examples.ko: 그 문제는 이번 회의에서 논외로 해요.
examples.en: Let's leave that issue out of this meeting.

examples.ko: 가격은 논외라면 이 가방이 제일 예뻐요.
examples.en: Setting the price aside, this bag is the prettiest.

examples.ko: 이건 논외의 이야기니까 나중에 다시 해요.
examples.en: This is off the topic, so let's talk about it again later.
In fact, that part was outside the discussion from the start.

examples.ko: 논외인 부분을 자꾸 이야기하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't keep talking about the parts that are beside the point.

examples.ko: 신입 사원 문제는 논외이니 일단 넘어가요.
examples.en: The new employee issue is outside the discussion, so let's move on for now.

explain: '논의'와 소리가 비슷해서 헷갈리는데, 논의는 '의논하는 것'이고 논외는 '논의하는 범위 밖'이에요. '논외로 하다', '논외로 치다'처럼 써서 어떤 것을 이야기에서 빼겠다고 말할 때 많이 써요. 반대로 '도마 위에 올리다'는 이야기 대상으로 삼는다는 말이에요.
explain_en: It sounds like '논의' (discussion) and is easily confused with it, but 논의 is discussing something, while 논외 is 'outside the scope of discussion'. It is used in '논외로 하다' and '논외로 치다' to say you will leave something out of the conversation. In contrast, '도마 위에 올리다' means to make something a subject of discussion.

examples.ko: 이번 토론의 논제가 너무 어려워서 준비하기 힘들어요.
examples.en: This debate's topic is so hard that it's tough to prepare.

examples.ko: 선생님이 발표 논제를 칠판에 적어 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher wrote the presentation topic on the board.
Please talk without straying from the topic.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 논제를 정하는 데만 하루가 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Our team spent a whole day just choosing the topic.
I looked up materials related to the topic at the library.

examples.ko: 오늘 논술 시험의 논제는 환경 문제였어요.
examples.en: The topic of today's essay exam was an environmental issue.

explain: '주제'와 비슷하지만 논제는 토론, 논술, 논문에서 따지고 이야기할 문제를 말할 때 써요. '논제를 정하다', '논제에서 벗어나다'처럼 학교나 회의에서 주로 나와요.
explain_en: It is similar to '주제' (theme), but 논제 is used for the question to be argued or discussed in debates, essays and papers. You will mostly hear it at school or in meetings, as in '논제를 정하다' or '논제에서 벗어나다'.

en: at once; immediately; on the spot; right away

examples.ko: 그 말을 듣고 단박에 화가 풀렸어요.
examples.en: My anger disappeared the moment I heard those words.
As soon as I saw the problem, I knew the answer right away.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 제 부탁을 단박에 거절했어요.
examples.en: He turned down my request on the spot.

examples.ko: 형은 단박에 일어나서 문을 열어 줬어요.
examples.en: My brother got up at once and opened the door for me.
Even though she said it was expensive, she bought it right away.

examples.ko: 단박에 마음에 드는 집을 찾아서 바로 계약했어요.
examples.en: I found a house I liked right away and signed the contract immediately.

explain: 거의 '단박에' 모양으로 써요. '바로', '당장'과 비슷하지만 망설임 없이 한 번에 해 버리는 느낌이 있어서, 결정하거나 이해하거나 거절할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It almost always appears as '단박에'. It is close to '바로' or '당장', but it carries a feel of doing something in one go without hesitation, so it suits deciding, understanding or refusing.

en: on earth; what in the world

examples.en: What on earth happened?
Who on earth did this?
How long on earth do I have to wait?
Gosh, how long has it been!
Tell me what on earth the problem is.
Where on earth did it all go wrong?

explain: 궁금하거나 답답한 마음을 강조하는 말이라 '도대체'와 비슷하지만, 좀 더 예스럽고 글 느낌이 나요. 일상 대화에서는 '도대체'나 '대체'를 더 많이 써요. 보통 의문문에서 써요.
explain_en: It stresses curiosity or frustration and is similar to '도대체', but it sounds more old-fashioned and bookish. In daily talk '도대체' or '대체' are more common. It is usually used in questions.

examples.en: Countless people have struggled because of this.
There were plenty of people who didn't know that shop.
Seoul has countless great restaurants, so it's hard to choose.
They say countless students failed the exam.
Mistakes like that happen all the time.

examples.ko: 영어를 배우다 포기한 사람이 부지기수인 걸요.
examples.en: There are so many people who gave up while learning English.

explain: '아주 많다'를 조금 격식 있게 말하는 표현이에요. 보통 '~이/가 부지기수예요' 모양으로 쓰고, 좋은 일이든 나쁜 일이든 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is a slightly formal way to say 'very many'. It is usually used as '~이/가 부지기수예요' and works for both good and bad things.

examples.en: I think there is no eternally unchanging truth in the world.
Trends don't stay fixed forever; they keep changing.

examples.ko: 법도 영구불변은 아니라서 시대에 따라 고쳐요.
examples.en: Laws are not fixed forever either, so they are revised over time.
It's hard to find anything truly eternal in reality.
Even things that seem unchanging will change someday.
No system remains unchanged forever.

explain: 한자어 네 글자라서 글이나 연설, 토론에서 주로 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '변하지 않는'이라고 풀어서 말해요. '영구불변의 진리'처럼 쓰거나, '영구불변은 없다'처럼 부정하는 문장에서 자주 써요.
explain_en: As a four-character Sino-Korean word, it mostly appears in writing, speeches and debates. In daily talk people say '변하지 않는' instead. It is used in phrases like '영구불변의 진리' or in negations such as '영구불변은 없다'.

examples.en: We discussed the new plan at the meeting.
In class, we discuss the topic in groups.
Everyone gathered, discussed ways, and decided.

examples.ko: 내일 토의할 내용을 미리 읽어 오세요.
examples.en: Please read tomorrow's discussion material beforehand.
If we discuss for long, good ideas come out.

examples.ko: 학생들이 쓰레기 문제를 토의하는 모습을 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched students discussing the garbage problem.

explain: '토의하다'는 답을 같이 찾으려고 의견을 나누는 거고, '토론하다'는 찬성과 반대로 나뉘어 논쟁하는 느낌이에요. 일상에서는 '이야기하다'가 흔하고, '토의하다'는 회의나 수업에서 써요.
explain_en: 토의하다 is exchanging opinions to find an answer together, while 토론하다 means arguing from opposing sides, closer to debate. In daily life 이야기하다 is the common choice; 토의하다 is for meetings and classes.

examples.en: Which school of thought does that philosopher belong to?

examples.ko: 두 학파는 같은 문제를 전혀 다르게 봤어요.
examples.en: The two schools saw the same problem in completely different ways.

examples.ko: 조선 후기에는 실학을 따르는 학파가 생겼어요.
examples.en: In the late Joseon period, a school that followed practical learning emerged.

examples.ko: 그 철학은 여러 학파로 나뉘어 발전했어요.
examples.en: That philosophy split into several schools and developed.

examples.ko: 같은 학파 출신끼리 모여서 연구회를 만들었어요.
examples.en: People from the same school of thought got together and formed a study group.
Do you know who the representative figures of the Northern Learning school are?

explain: '학교'와 달리 건물이나 기관이 아니라 같은 생각이나 방법을 따르는 학자들의 무리를 가리켜요. '실학파', '북학파'처럼 이름 뒤에 붙여 써요. 철학, 경제학, 미술, 역사 이야기에서 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Unlike '학교', it is not a building or institution but a group of scholars who share the same ideas or methods. It attaches to a name, as in '실학파' and '북학파'. It often comes up when talking about philosophy, economics, art and history.

examples.en: The walls of the country house were made of red clay.

examples.ko: 비가 온 뒤에 황토 길이 질척거렸어요.
examples.en: After the rain, the red clay road was muddy.
Sweating in a red clay sauna feels refreshing.
The kids ran around barefoot on the red clay.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 황토가 많아서 고구마가 잘 자라요.
examples.en: This area has a lot of red clay, so sweet potatoes grow well.

examples.ko: 황토 팩을 얼굴에 바르고 십 분 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I put a red clay pack on my face and waited ten minutes.

explain: '황토'는 붉은빛이 도는 누런 흙이에요. 한국에서는 몸에 좋은 흙이라는 생각이 있어서 집, 찜질방, 화장품에 많이 써요. 그냥 흙은 '흙'이라고 하고, '황토'는 이런 특별한 흙을 가리켜요.
explain_en: 황토 is reddish-yellow soil. In Korea it is seen as healthy soil, so it appears in houses, saunas, and cosmetics. Ordinary soil is just 흙, while 황토 points to this special kind.

examples.en: Parents' ways of disciplining differ from home to home.

examples.ko: 아이를 훈육할 때는 화내지 않는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: When you discipline a child, it's important not to get angry.

examples.ko: 엄격한 훈육이 꼭 좋은 것은 아니에요.
examples.en: Strict discipline is not necessarily a good thing.
At school, they emphasize conversation more than discipline.

examples.ko: 사랑 없는 훈육은 아이에게 상처가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Discipline without love can hurt a child.
Discipline and corporal punishment are completely different.

explain: '교육'보다 아이의 행동과 예절을 바로잡아 주는 데 초점이 있어요. 육아나 교육 이야기에서 '훈육 방식', '훈육이 필요하다'처럼 자주 써요. 일상에서는 '버릇을 가르치다', '혼내다'라고도 말하지만, '혼내다'는 야단치는 느낌이 더 강해요.
explain_en: Compared with '교육' (education), it focuses on correcting a child's behavior and manners. It is common in parenting and education talk, as in '훈육 방식' or '훈육이 필요하다'. In daily speech people also say '버릇을 가르치다' or '혼내다', but '혼내다' sounds more like scolding.
